A feature release that syncs the SDK with Python SDK v0.2.182 (from v0.2.168).
Hooks can now block an action when they fail instead of letting it run, and
results report the uuids of the prompts they answer. Session reads return a
turn with parallel tool calls whole, and the SDK now stops a callback when the
CLI cancels the request behind it. Some failures that used to be silent now
stop `connect()`; read the first section before upgrading.

## ⚠️ Behavior and compatibility changes

**`settings` that can't be merged with `sandbox` now fail `connect()`**
([Python #1426](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/pull/1426)).
When both are set, the SDK reads the settings and merges the sandbox into them.
Before, a settings file that was missing, unreadable or not valid JSON was
logged, and the CLI started with only the sandbox settings: your permission
rules and hooks were silently gone. Now `connect()` throws
`CLIConnectionException("Failed to load settings: ...")`.

- It covers a missing file, a directory, invalid JSON (inline or in a file),
  JSON that is not an object, and content after the object.
- The message gives the line and column of a JSON error but never quotes the
  settings text, which can hold secrets.
- A relative settings path now resolves against `cwd` when `cwd` is set, as
  the CLI resolves it, and a UTF-8 byte-order mark is stripped.
- Without `sandbox`, the value still goes to `--settings` unchanged.

**Windows CLI discovery finds only `claude.exe`, and only in absolute `PATH`
entries** ([Python #1484](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/pull/1484)).
Relative entries (`""`, `.`, `tools`) resolve against the working directory,
where someone else could plant a binary, so they are skipped. The fallback to
`~/.local/bin/claude.exe` stays.

- Without `allowUnsafeWindowsBatchCli(true)`, npm's `claude.cmd` shim and
  extensionless git-bash/WSL wrappers are no longer returned as a last resort.
  On such a machine the SDK now throws `CLINotFoundException`, whose message
  points at the native installer. Before, `connect()` failed with the
  batch-script refusal or a spawn error.
- **Java only:** with `allowUnsafeWindowsBatchCli(true)`, discovery still
  returns `claude.cmd`, then `claude.bat`, from an absolute `PATH` entry when no
  `claude.exe` exists, so callers who opted in keep auto-discovery. The Python
  SDK has no such opt-in.
- A path passed with `cliPath(...)` is used as given.

**New record components.** `AssistantMessage`, `ResultMessage` and
`StreamEvent` gain `userMessageUuid` and `userMessageUuids`, and `HookMatcher`
gains `onFailure`. Every previous constructor signature is kept, so source that
calls `new` compiles unchanged. Record deconstruction patterns on JDK 21+
(`case ResultMessage(var a, ...)`) must add the new components, and code
compiled against the old canonical constructors needs a recompile.

**The CLI version check no longer runs `claude -v`**
([Python #1483](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/pull/1483)).
The version is read from the first `system`/`init` message, so `cliPath` is
executed only to start the session. A CLI too old to report its version gets
one warning naming its path, and the too-old warning now goes only to the
logger, no longer also to `System.err`. `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK`
still turns the check off.

## Highlights

**Hooks that fail closed: `HookMatcher.onFailure`**
([Python #1460](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/pull/1460)).
By default a hook that fails counts as no decision, so the action goes ahead.
The new `HookOnFailure.BLOCK` policy blocks it instead, which is what a
security guard needs:

```java
new HookMatcher("Bash|PowerShell", List.of(checkCommand), null, HookOnFailure.BLOCK)
```

- A callback fails when its future completes exceptionally, it completes with
  `null`, it returns a `null` future, or the CLI rejects what it returns. A
  callback with no opinion should return `HookOutput.empty()`.
- With a `BLOCK` matcher, `connect()` throws `CLIConnectionException` if the
  CLI doesn't report `hook_on_failure_supported` (too old to honor the policy)
  or reports `hooks_applied: false` (a running session that didn't register the
  hooks). Either way the guard would otherwise fail open or never run.
- `Hooks.java` puts its dangerous-command guard on `BLOCK` and covers both
  `Bash` and `PowerShell`.

**Find the result for your prompt: `userMessageUuid()` / `userMessageUuids()`**
([Python #1505](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/pull/1505)).
In streaming-input mode, `origin()` tells you what started a turn but not
whether it answers *your* prompt: a prompt sent while an injected turn runs can
be answered inside that turn. Send each prompt as a message map with a fresh
top-level `uuid` and look for it on the results:

```java
List<String> uuids = result.userMessageUuids() != null ? result.userMessageUuids() : List.of();
if (myUuid.equals(result.userMessageUuid()) || uuids.contains(myUuid)) {
    // this turn took in the prompt sent with myUuid
}
```

The fields are also set on `AssistantMessage` and `StreamEvent`. An empty list
(an interrupted turn) stays distinct from `null` (no uuid, or an older CLI).
Error results carry the uuid too, so check `isError()` before treating the
prompt as answered. `MessageOriginExample` runs the round trip.

**Cancelled control requests are honored**
([Python #751](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/pull/751)).
When the CLI abandons a hook call, a `canUseTool` check or an SDK MCP message
(for example when a turn is interrupted), it sends `control_cancel_request`.
Earlier releases ignored it, so the callback ran on and its answer went to a
CLI that no longer expected it. Now the SDK:

- cancels the callback's `CompletableFuture`, so work composed on it can stop;
- interrupts the thread waiting on it, which also reaches a callback that
  blocks its own thread;
- cancels an SDK MCP tool's `ToolCallContext`, as `notifications/cancelled`
  does; and
- sends no response.

A request ends either answered or cancelled, never both, so a cancel cannot cut
into a response being written.

**Session reads return a parallel tool turn whole**
([Python #1422](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/pull/1422)).
The CLI writes a response with N parallel tool calls as N assistant entries,
each with its own result, so the transcript forks. `getSessionMessages()` and
`getSessionMessagesFromStore()` followed one branch and dropped the other calls
and results. Both now put them back, every result after its call. The new
`ParallelToolSessionReadsExample` runs such a turn against the live CLI and
checks both readers.

**`ClaudeAgentOptions.clientApp(String)`**
([Python #1432](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/pull/1432)).
Identifies your app or library on API requests (e.g. `"my-app/1.0.0"`) by
setting `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_CLIENT_APP` for the CLI. It wins over `env` and the
inherited value; `""` sends none. Unlike Python, the SDK derives no default
label, since it ships no bundled CLI.

## Also in this release

- **Session paging fixed.** `getSessionMessagesFromStore` and
  `getSubagentMessagesFromStore` applied `limit` before `offset`, so
  `limit=3, offset=4` returned nothing. Every reader now returns messages
  `offset` to `offset + limit - 1`, and `getSessionMessages` treats `limit=0`
  as no limit instead of returning an empty list.
- **Branch selection in session reads matches the Python SDK.** The latest
  main-chain leaf wins, then the latest leaf of any kind. A trailing meta entry
  could previously pick an older branch, and a transcript ending in a sidechain
  lost its tail. Malformed `uuid`/`parentUuid` values are skipped instead of
  throwing `ClassCastException`.
- **`settingSources` Javadoc** explains the `null` default (every source
  loads) and using `List.of()` to isolate a session when `cwd` may be
  untrusted, since project settings can run hooks
  ([Python #1486](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/pull/1486)).
- **Documentation:** the hooks, message-type, session, configuration and
  transport pages cover all of the above, in English and the five
  translations. Eleven snippets that looped over `receiveMessages()` with a
  for-each, and five that called a nonexistent `StreamEvent.delta()`, now
  compile.
- **Tests:** 1224. New suites cover `onFailure` and its CLI checks,
  control-request cancellation, parallel-tool session reads and paging,
  user-message uuid parsing, and the settings, client-app and version-check
  transport changes. All examples were run against Claude Code 2.1.325.
